what: PieBot's multi-threaded search was not merely failing to scale -- it was actively losing games. The root-split implementation compared fail-soft bounds across a racing shared alpha to choose the root move. Replacing it with Lazy SMP is +129 Elo at 4 threads.
headline: Multi-threaded search measured -161 Elo vs single-threaded. Lazy SMP makes it +95.

the_defect.location: PieBot/src/search/alphabeta.rs, fn search_depth_parallel (deleted in this change, 341 lines)
shape: Each tail root move read `let local_alpha = alpha_shared.load(Relaxed)` ONCE, then scouted with a null window `(-local_alpha - 1, -local_alpha)`.
A null-window scout that fails low returns a fail-soft UPPER BOUND, not a score. The true value can be arbitrarily worse.
Other threads kept raising `alpha_shared` concurrently, so different moves were scouted against DIFFERENT alphas -- their returned bounds are not on a common scale.
The aggregation then chose the root move with `if score > best_score { bestmove = Some(m) }`, comparing those incomparable bounds as if they were exact scores.

`abort.store(true)` on a beta cutoff cancelled in-flight workers whose results were silently dropped (`Err(Cancelled) => {}`), which can remove the genuinely best move from the comparison and leave a bogus fail-low bound as the winner.
the_defect.consequence: The engine could return a root move it never verified. More nodes bought worse moves.

measurements.harness: PieBot/src/bin/compare_play.rs, --movetime 200 --noise-plies 12 --noise-topk 5, colours alternated, serial play (the harness forces one game at a time whenever either side uses >1 thread).
measurements.note_on_a_discarded_run: A first 60-game run was killed and re-run: `cargo test` had been launched concurrently, and a 200 ms-per-move comparison is meaningless when the test suite is saturating every core. Only the quiet-machine runs are reported here.

head_to_head_both_4T.comment: The decisive run: identical thread count on both sides, so the ONLY difference is root-split vs Lazy SMP.

measurements.ci_method: Normal approximation on the per-game score distribution, NOT the paired bootstrap the promotion protocol prefers. Pairing can only tighten these intervals, and every lower bound already clears zero by a wide margin, so the promotion decision does not depend on the difference.

the_fix.design: Lazy SMP. Helper searchers run their own complete iterative deepening on the same root, sharing only the `Arc<Tt>`. Half are skewed one iteration ahead so the pool spreads across the depth schedule. Nothing reads a helper's score -- helpers contribute exclusively through the entries they leave in the TT -- so no fail-soft bound ever reaches a comparison it cannot support. Only the main thread's result is reported.
applied_to_both_id_loops: `search_movetime` -- used by the compare_play harness and one UCI path.
`search_with_params` -- used by the real UCI `go` handler (uci.rs:651). The original root split fed this path too, so fixing only `search_movetime` would have left the production path broken.
the_fix.eligibility: threads > 1 && !deterministic && node_limit == u64::MAX && (!use_nnue || nnue_quant.is_some()). At threads == 1 the helper count is 0 and the code path is unchanged.
the_fix.prior_art_note: `search_movetime_lazy_smp` already existed in the file but was a stub forwarding to `search_movetime`, and nothing called it. The name predated the implementation.

single_threaded_is_bit_identical.correction_to_the_handoff: CLAUDE.md records `accept_temp 11742536 when the fork is the stub`. That is wrong: the stub measures 11763048. The two binaries use different option sets (`opts=alphabeta` vs `opts=(default)`), so their node counts are not comparable to each other and never were. Each must be compared only against its own history.

roadmap_target.root_split: 2.47x -- never met, and the Elo was negative anyway

caveats: All Elo here is at 200 ms/move on an Apple-silicon Mac. Per the 2026-08-16 finding that the short-time-control harness understates depth-dependent changes ~2.3x, the true SMP gain at longer time controls is plausibly larger, but that is an extrapolation, not a measurement.

Measured at 4 threads only. 8T and higher are untested, and Lazy SMP is known to scale sublinearly past ~8 threads without additional diversification (varied aspiration windows, per-thread move-ordering noise).

UNRESOLVED AND POSSIBLY DECISIVE FOR PRIORITISATION: it is unconfirmed whether the CCRL 40/15 main list gives each engine one core or all four. If one core, this fix is worth nothing on that specific list -- though it still turns multi-core play from -161 Elo into a gain, which matters for every other use. Attempts to verify failed: computerchess.org.uk returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches and ccrl.chessdom.com did not resolve.
